title: The Patient Is Always Right? Evaluating Sycophancy in Medical Diagnosis with Graded Patient Beliefs
abstract: arXiv:2610.34013v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: More people are seeking out general-purpose AI models for medical advice, including diagnosis. Yet, AI models are susceptible to sycophancy, like validating users' beliefs even when they are untrue, which could lead to false positive diagnoses. Here, we evaluate how nine AI models change their diagnostic decision when a patient presents a belief that they have a specific (but incorrect) medical condition. We vary how close the user belief is to the clinical evidence presented. Models sycophantically adopt the patient's belief on average 23.2\% of the time---sometimes even when the patient proposes a fictional, made-up condition. We also varied different personas, including a Rare Disease Claimer that got models to accept their belief 43.0\% of the time. translated_title: 患者总是对的吗？基于分级患者信念的医学诊断谄媚行为评估
translated_abstract: 越来越多的人开始向通用AI模型寻求医疗建议，包括诊断。然而，AI模型容易受到谄媚行为的影响，例如即使知道用户的信念不真实，也会对其进行附和验证，这可能导致假阳性诊断。本研究评估了当患者声称自己患有某种特定（但不正确）的疾病时，九个AI模型会如何改变其诊断决策。我们改变了用户信念与所呈现临床证据之间的接近程度。结果显示，模型平均有23.2%的概率会谄媚地采纳患者的信念——有时即使患者提出的是一个虚构的、根本不存在的疾病，模型也会附和。我们还测试了不同的人物设定，其中一种“罕见疾病声称者”设定使模型接受其信念的概率高达43.0%。附加分析发现，经过医学领域微调以及规模更大的模型更不容易改变其原有诊断。医学诊断中的谄媚偏差引发了……
tldr: 该研究评估了九个AI模型在医学诊断中的谄媚行为，发现模型平均23.2%的情况下会附和患者错误的自诊信念（甚至包括虚构疾病），而医学微调和更大的模型规模可降低这种易感性。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates sycophancy in medical diagnosis across nine AI models, finding that models adopt patients' incorrect self-diagnostic beliefs 23.2% of the time on average—even fabricated conditions—with medical fine-tuning and larger model scale reducing susceptibility.
